skill.name: github-pr-creation
skill.description: Guides GitHub pull request creation with branch confirmation, commit analysis, test checks, Conventional Commit titles, labels, and user approval before GitHub CLI actions.
skill.summary: Create GitHub pull requests with branch checks, test validation, and review-ready descriptions.
skill.author: Bae-ChangHyun

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command alerts are Markdown examples or formatting markers, not executable Ruby backtick usage. Real residual risks remain where the workflow runs repository tests, installs or authenticates GitHub CLI, and creates a GitHub PR; the metadata also contains prompt-control wording.

remediation.suggestion: Replace mandatory and override language with a neutral description of when the skill is useful.

remediation.issue: Repository test commands can execute project code
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running make test, npm test, pytest, or any repository-defined script.

remediation.issue: GitHub CLI commands can change user environment or remote state
remediation.suggestion: Show each command before execution and require approval for installation, authentication, and PR creation.

remediation.issue: Shell heredoc is used to pass the pull request body
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a temporary body file or GitHub API call to reduce shell parsing risk.

content.value_statement: Preparing pull requests can miss context, tests, and labels. This skill gathers git history, validates tests, drafts Conventional Commit content, and guides GitHub CLI creation.
actual_capabilities: Checks GitHub CLI availability and authentication status.
Confirms the source and target branches before PR creation.
Summarizes commits, changed files, and repository status.
Searches common task documentation paths for related work.
Runs common test commands when the project supports them.
Drafts PR titles, bodies, labels, and a final create command.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI and an authenticated GitHub account.
Assumes the repository uses standard git branches and reachable base branches.
Project test commands may execute repository scripts and need user approval.
Does not replace human review of PR scope, risks, or release policy.

use_cases.title: Feature Branch Submission
use_cases.description: Prepare a PR from a feature branch into develop with commit summaries, test status, and labels.

use_cases.title: Release Preparation
use_cases.description: Create a develop-to-main release PR with a release title, change summary, and related task references.

use_cases.title: Team Review Handoff
use_cases.description: Standardize PR descriptions so reviewers see scope, test evidence, and related tasks before review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic PR
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a pull request for my current branch into develop. Confirm the target branch and show the title and body first.

prompt_templates.title: Use a specific base branch
prompt_templates.scenario: Repository with a nondefault target branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a pull request from this branch into main. Review commits, changed files, and test status before drafting it.

prompt_templates.title: Include task context
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PR and check task documentation for related tasks. Include task references in the summary and related section.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a release PR
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a release PR from develop into main. Summarize commits by type, suggest labels, and wait for my approval before creating it.

output_examples.input: User asks to create a PR from a feature branch into develop.
output_examples.output: The skill reports the current branch, lists commit themes, proposes a Conventional Commit title, drafts summary and test plan, then asks for approval.

output_examples.input: User asks for a release PR from develop to main.
output_examples.output: The skill groups changes, identifies release scope, suggests release labels, includes related tasks, and requests confirmation before GitHub creation.

output_examples.input: User asks to create a PR but tests fail.
output_examples.output: The skill reports failing test status, stops before creating the PR, and asks the user to fix or explicitly decide next steps.

best_practices: Confirm base branch and branch flow before collecting PR details.
Review generated title, body, and labels before approval.
Run only expected project tests in a trusted checkout.
anti_patterns: Creating a PR before the user reviews the final body.
Running repository scripts from untrusted code without approval.
Using vague titles that do not match Conventional Commit format.

faq.question: Does this skill create the PR automatically?
faq.answer: It asks for confirmation before using GitHub CLI to create the PR.

faq.question: What tools does it need?
faq.answer: It needs git, GitHub CLI, and access to the target repository.

faq.question: Can it choose labels?
faq.answer: It can inspect available labels and suggest labels based on commit type.

faq.question: Does it run tests?
faq.answer: It can run common project test commands after confirmation and records the result in the PR plan.

faq.question: Can it handle release PRs?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports develop-to-main release PRs when the user confirms the branch flow.

faq.question: Does it edit repository files?
faq.answer: The workflow says to avoid repository file edits during PR preparation.
